references.text: Israel made a vow to the Lord to devote the Canaanite cities to destruction if God gave them victory, a conditional vow similar to the one Jephthah made.
The law concerning vows to the Lord states that when someone makes a vow to the Lord, they must not break their word but do everything they have promised.
Jacob made a conditional vow to the Lord, following a structure similar to Jephthah's vow with 'if... then I will'.
Hannah made a conditional vow to the Lord to give her son to Him if she was granted a son, a vow similar to Jephthah's.
The Preacher warns about being careful with vows to God and fulfilling what one promises, which is relevant to Jephthah's rash vow.
The law on vows requires that a vow made to the Lord must be fulfilled without delay, for the Lord will require it of you.
Jephthah is mentioned among the heroes of faith who by faith conquered kingdoms, referring to his victory over the Ammonites.
